verdict.rationale: Sumsub documents a drop-in WebSDK, with React and mobile SDKs, that is initialized with an access token the developer generates. It also offers hosted WebSDK permalinks for a redirect flow, and verification levels that bundle document and selfie/liveness steps, so no capture UI has to be built. Results come back through webhooks, WebSDK event messages and the REST API. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration, and explicit documentation that the token is created server-side and of the result-retrieval API call.

support.subject: As a developer, I can launch a complete document-plus-selfie verification with a hosted or drop-in flow — create a session server-side, redirect or embed, and read the result — without building capture UI myself

citations.quote: Generate an access token to be passed to the WebSDK during initialization.
WebSDK permalinks help applicants pass verification via a direct link to the WebSDK.
Each level may include document-based or selfie-based verification, Liveness & Face match
Sumsub’s Webhooks is a tool that allows you to automatically receive notifications for various events and changes related to your applicants’ verification process.
the WebSDK sends event messages for key moments in the verification flow — status changes, applicant actions, and more
